signals.title: CHF/JPY — G10 Bilateral Theme + Carry Divergence
signals.text: CHF/JPY trades at 188.805, reflecting broad franc underperformance against the yen. JPY leads the G10 strength scorecard with a 1W average of +1.090% across 7 pairs, while CHF lags at -0.730% across 6 pairs, generating a critical 1.820% bilateral spread. This divergence unfolds despite a 125bp policy rate advantage favoring JPY (BoJ 1.25% vs SNB 0.00%), which exerts steady structural downside pressure on the cross. In the options space, elevated demand for downside protection persists with JPY puts heavily bid, as seen in USD/JPY 25d RR at -2.57. Trade bias: Bearish CHF/JPY; bilateral divergence supported by the 125bp JPY rate premium. Catalyst: Japan Industrial Production and BoJ Summary of Opinions at 23:50 UTC. Risk: Leader-to-laggard spread compresses below 0.80% as CHF recovers.

signals.title: AUD/USD — CB Rhetoric + Crowded Long Caution
signals.text: AUD/USD trades at 0.6986, holding below its SMA20/50/200 cluster (0.7134, 0.7096, and 0.7028). RBA Governor Bullock stated the board considered both a pause and a 25bp hike today, noting that inflation progress means four prior hikes may prove restrictive enough to halt further tightening. CFTC data shows leveraged funds net long +55,684 contracts (81st percentile of the 52-week range), but the WoW delta stalled at -3,615 contracts as buyers hesitate. While RBA 4.60% vs Fed 4.00% maintains a 60bp AUD carry premium (AONIA vs SOFR at -45bp), Bullock's balanced forward guidance caps upside follow-through. Trade bias: Neutral AUD/USD; positioning exhaustion counteracts nominal carry advantage. Catalyst: Australia Building Approvals and Trade Balance at 01:30 UTC. Risk: Reclaiming the SMA200 at 0.7028 invalidates near-term consolidation.
evidence: RBA Gov. Bullock: considered pause and 25-bps hike

signals.title: USD/CAD — Retail Extreme + Real Yield Divergence
signals.text: USD/CAD trades at 1.4192, positioned comfortably above its rising SMA20/50/200 cluster at 1.3943, 1.3949, and 1.3843. Retail positioning shows an extreme 94% short bias on Retail sentiment data, directly contradicting institutional positioning where leveraged funds remain net short CAD (-49,123 contracts, 69th percentile). The pair draws fundamental support from a 175bp Fed-BoC policy differential (Fed 4.00% vs BoC 2.25%, with SOFR vs CORRA spread at +160bp in favor of USD). Furthermore, US 5Y yields rose +25bp over 5D (FRED, as of Sep 24) led by a +24bp surge in real yields, reinforcing broad dollar demand against retail contrarians. Trade bias: Bullish USD/CAD; structural carry and retail short squeeze favor upside continuation. Catalyst: Canada GDP and US Core PCE at 12:30 UTC. Risk: Daily close below the SMA20 at 1.3943 invalidates the bullish structure.
evidence: Fed 4.00% vs BoC 2.25% — +175bp carry favors USD

signals.title: USD/JPY — Options Downside Skew + Vol Compression
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 157.38, holding above its SMA20 (156.28) but capped beneath the SMA50 and SMA200 resistance band at 158.49/158.45. Options pricing reflects significant protection demand against spot weakness, with the 1M 25-delta Risk Reversal printing at -2.57 (Saxo indicative mid), marking an extreme put skew. At the same time, ATM implied volatility stands at 9.1% against 30-day realized volatility of 10.1%, yielding a negative vol risk premium of -1.1% that indicates pricing complacency. Fed 4.00% vs BoJ 1.25% provides a substantial 275bp carry cushion (+267bp on SOFR vs TONA), yet the heavy options put skew flags institutional hedging against downside breaks. Trade bias: Range-bound USD/JPY; wide carry support collides with downside options hedging. Catalyst: BoJ Summary of Opinions and Tankan Survey at 23:50 UTC. Risk: Sustained breakout above 158.50 forces put-protection unwinds.
evidence: Fed 4.00% vs BoJ 1.25% — +275bp carry favors USD
